newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Calendar call spread bought in BG.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Calendar call spread bought in BG.

text.p: A neutral to bullish call spread was taken in BG Plc on Wednesday, in one of the largest deals of the day, as interest in UK equity options stepped up in line with the underlying market.
A June/December 200 call spread was traded for a combined cost of 6-1/2p for 1,000 contracts.
This calendar or time spread, involves the sale of one option and the simulataneous purchase of a more distant option, both with the same striking price.

The strategy is based on the premise that time will erode the value of the near-term option at a faster rate than it will the far-term option. The spread may widen and a profit may result at near-term expiration.

It is not necessary for the underlying price in BG to be exactly at the striking price of 200p for a profit to result. Some profit can be made in a range that extends both below and above the strike price.

The risk in this type of position is that the stock will drop sharply or rise a great deal, in which case the spread between the two options will shrink and the investor will lose money. But since the spread between the two calls cannot shrink to less than zero, the risk is limited to the amount of the 6-1/2p original debit, plus commissions.
Shares in BG were trading unchanged at 181-1/2p.
In FTSE index options, one bullish investor bought around 4,500 June 4,600 calls for 23p.
"This deal was market sensitive, it helped the market perk up this morning," one dealer said.
Another large deal executed on Tuesday involved 12,000 lots in May 4,575 calls bought at 2p.
The FTSE was trading almost 40 points higher on Wednesday at 4,385.4, after earlier coming within reach of the 4,400 level. An overnight 174-point surge on the Dow had lifted sentiment.
The dealer could close the position now to realise a profit of 2p per contract or 240,000 stg excluding commissions.
"that's what you call a quick turn," one trader commented.
